subject: Hospitality
title: Thomas Cook: Inventing Tourism
description: A quick, practical guide to Thomas Cook: Inventing Tourism.

hook.text: Thomas Cook organized the world's first package tour in 1841—a train trip for 570 temperance supporters in England.

buildup.text: Cook bundled transport, accommodation, and guided services into one price. Travelers no longer arranged each piece themselves.

discovery.text: He invented the 'circular note'—a precursor to traveler's checks—so tourists didn't have to carry large sums of foreign cash.

twist.text: Cook made travel accessible to the middle class. Before him, international travel was only for the wealthy and adventurous.

climax.text: Thomas Cook & Son became the world's largest travel company. The packaged tourism concept he invented still drives the industry.

punchline.text: One train trip for 570 people. Thomas Cook invented modern tourism.

quiz.question: What did Thomas Cook invent in 1841?
options: The world's first package tour—bundling transport and accommodation
